newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Kabila says he has no designs on Zaire presidency.
newsitem.headline: Kabila says he has no designs on Zaire presidency.

text.p: Rebel leader Laurent Kabila, his popularity soaring with each new battlefield victory, says he has no designs on Zaire's presidency.
"I am not the liberator. I participated in the rebellion, but I don't want to be president," he told a news conference in Zaire's third city of Kisangani on Saturday.
"I want my people to be free and then I will return to my private life."
Kabila, whose forces control a fifth of the huge Central African nation, outlined his plans for a transitional government -- saying any transition should last no more than a year.
But he ruled out working with any politician who had shared power with ailing veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko, who returned to the capital on Friday to salvage what remains of his authority.
He said a transitional government should include members of his Alliance for Democratic Forces for the Liberation Congo/Zaire (ADFL), but he added:
"We say that the ADFL transitional government should be made of ADFL members and only anti-Mobutists and anti-regime people who have never been in power and who never shared power."
Mobutu, 66, seized power in 1965 but many ordinary Zaireans, eager for a change from three decades of poverty and hardship under his rule, are openly rallying to Kabila.
Before leaving France for home, Mobutu called for a truce and talks and the creation of a national council to find ways out of the crisis "with all our brothers, without exclusion".
Kabila and a roaring crowd of 10,000 supporters firmly told U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun on Saturday there would be no cease-fire with the government before negotiations.
Sahnoun, trying to broker a peace deal, left Kisangani after brief talks with Kabila.

The rebels took up arms in October in a dispute about Zairean nationality for an ethnic Tutsi minority, who form the core of Kabila's fighting force. An alliance of anti-Mobutu groups rallied to the cause.
Mobutu has spent most of his time in Europe since August, and has had prostate cancer surgery there. He left hospital in Monaco on Wednesday after a fresh bout of cancer treatment.
He returned home from France on Friday on his private jet but has not been seen in public since climbing abroad the plane in Nice. He stayed out of the public eye on Saturday.
South Africa's deputy president, Thabo Mbeki, flies to Kinshasa on Sunday for talks with Mobutu on the peace moves.

The United States and Belgium, meanwhile, sent or prepared to send troops to countries neighbouring Zaire in anticipation of any need to evacuate their citizens. France has already sent troops to Congo and Gabon for the same reason.
